# Diagnosis
Before you can treat a patient you need to know what's wrong. How much you can see depends on your medical training.
## Looking at the Patient - [bold]Examining[/bold] someone shows their visible wounds and fractures, and which body part each one is on. - [bold]Inspect injuries[/bold]: right-click a patient and choose Inspect injuries to take a closer look. After a short check you get an injury report listing each body part's wounds and how badly they're bleeding. You can bind a key to this under [bold]CMU Medical[/bold] in the controls menu.
## The Health Analyzer Use it on a patient to open a full scan. - [bold]Top bar[/bold]: overall health, pulse, blood level, temperature and shock risk, with a status of stable, serious, critical or deceased. - [bold]Body[/bold]: each body part's health, with its wounds, bleeding, embedded shrapnel, eschar, splints, casts and tourniquets. - [bold]Bleeding[/bold]: with basic medical training, the scan shows how bad each bleed is (minor, moderate, severe or [color=red]arterial[/color]), on the blood readout and on each bleeding body part. A missing limb's row shows whether its stump is bleeding arterially or has a tourniquet on it. - [bold]Fractures and internal bleeding[/bold]: need basic medical training. With more training it tells you the exact fracture severity and where the bleeding is. - [bold]Organs[/bold]: need a trained medic. Each organ shows its stage (healthy, bruised, damaged, failing or dead) and health. - [bold]Pain[/bold]: the patient's pain level and how close they are to pain shock. - For a dead patient it also shows roughly how many minutes are left before they can no longer be brought back.
If the analyzer can't show something because of your training, it says so, so you know to find someone more qualified rather than assuming the patient is fine.
## Damage Types The analyzer breaks a patient's damage down by type. Each group heals differently, so knowing which one you're looking at tells you what to reach for.
[bold]Brute[/bold]: blunt, slash and piercing. Punches, claws, blades and bullets. - Dress the wounds with gauze or a trauma kit, then heal with [bold]bicaridine[/bold]. - Heavy brute damage can also break bones and cause internal bleeding. - See [textlink="Brute Medications" link="CMUGuideMedsBrute"].
[bold]Burn[/bold]: heat, shock, cold and caustic. Fire, electricity, freezing and acid. - Treat the burns with ointment or a burn kit, then heal with [bold]kelotane[/bold] or the stronger [bold]dermaline[/bold]. - A big burn in one hit can leave eschar. See [textlink="Wounds and Bleeding" link="CMUGuideMedicalWounds"]. - See [textlink="Burn Medications" link="CMUGuideMedsBurn"].
[bold]Toxin[/bold]: poison and radiation. Toxic chemicals, overdoses, failing organs and radiation. - Heal with [bold]dylovene[/bold], which also clears hallucinations. - Keep an eye on the liver and kidneys, which filter toxins and get damaged by them. See [textlink="Organs" link="CMUGuideMedicalOrgans"]. - See [textlink="Toxin Medications" link="CMUGuideMedsToxin"].
[bold]Suffocation[/bold]: asphyxiation and blood loss. Not breathing, damaged lungs, a stopped heart, or bleeding out. - Heal with [bold]dexalin[/bold], and breathe from an oxygen tank to recover three times as fast. - Blood loss won't go away until the blood is replaced. Stop the bleeding and give blood. - See [textlink="Suffocation Medications" link="CMUGuideMedsSuffocation"].
[bold]Genetic[/bold]: cellular damage. Rare, and only a few things cause it. - Only a few treatments touch it, such as [bold]cryoxadone[/bold] in a cryo pod. See [textlink="Other Medications" link="CMUGuideMedsOther"].
[bold]Tricordrazine[/bold] heals a little of brute, burn, toxin and suffocation all at once, and is a good general-purpose drug when you're not sure what you're dealing with. For every medicine, see [textlink="Medications" link="CMUGuideMedications"].
## The Stethoscope Use it on a patient, or right-click them, and listen for 2 seconds. It needs basic medical training. - [bold]Heart[/bold]: whether there's a heartbeat, and how fast. A trained medic hears the exact rate. - [bold]Lungs[/bold]: you hear the patient breathe: - [bold]Clear[/bold]: healthy lungs. - [bold]Wet[/bold]: crackling breaths. Fluid or blood in the lungs, from pulmonary edema or lung damage. - [bold]Faint[/bold]: quiet, weak breaths. The lungs are failing and barely moving air. - A dead patient isn't breathing, so there's nothing to hear. - A trained medic can also tell how much pain the patient is in.
## Holocards Patients get a holocard automatically, based on their condition: - [bold]Stable[/bold]: only minor injuries. - [bold]Trauma[/bold]: fractures or internal bleeding. - [bold]Organ failure[/bold]: at least one organ is failing.
## Body Scanner The [bold]body scanner pod[/bold] and its console give a full scan of a patient lying in the pod, including enclosed injuries, and help plan surgery. See [textlink="Medical Machines" link="CMUGuideMedicalMachines"].
## Patient Monitor A Lifepak can be hooked up to a patient to watch their heart rhythm, oxygen, blood pressure and more in real time. See [textlink="Defibrillators" link="CMUGuideDefibrillators"].
